rationale: C18 plausibly supplied a material structural template: both memoranda analyze an old private claim that failed because a statutory limitations period expired, distinguish procedural disposition from adjudication on the merits, assess whether equitable circumstances justify special relief, and focus on a jurisdictional enactment waiving the limitations bar so a court can determine the claim. The child adapts that machinery but rejects the particular bill because it both lacks sufficient equitable justification and dictates the tax-computation method. C11 and C20 contain similar jurisdictional-waiver alternatives, but their factual and procedural structures are less closely aligned with the child's prior litigation and limitations history.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Since the bill grants relief from the operation of the statute of limitation, special equitable circumstances should appear which require that this taxpayer be singled out for special relief.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I also agree with the Veterans' Administration that the case does not present any equitable consideration which warrants the direct gratuity award proposed.
shared_material.explanation: Both make equitable justification the central test for exceptional private legislation overcoming ordinary legal rules.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Even assuming the desirability of granting jurisdiction to the Court of Claims for this year, it does not seem desirable to preclude the Court from determining the correct tax liability for the year.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I believe, therefore, that in fairness to Mrs. McQuilkin she is entitled to a day in court for decision of her claim on its merits, and I would be willing to approve a jurisdictional enactment waiving the bar of any statute of limitations.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same judicial-remedy machinery: waive the limitations bar and leave the substantive merits for judicial determination.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The claim for refund filed in 1933 was rejected on the grounds it was not filed within the statutory period.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The lower court decision, however, was reversed on appeal to the Circuit Court of Appeals on the ground that the statutory period of limitations for filing such a suit had expired.
shared_material.explanation: Each builds the memorandum around an aged claim whose merits were not finally resolved because the claimant missed a statutory deadline.
